disclaimer: Research demo only — not medical advice. These are sample hardcoded tips for the XBDS2024N deployment prototype. Always consult a qualified clinician or pharmacist before changing medication.

High.title: High perceived effectiveness
High.recommendation: Sample tip: Keep a short symptom diary of what improved and for how long. Share this with your clinician at the next review so they can decide whether to maintain the current plan. Do not change dose on your own.

Moderate.title: Moderate / partial response
Moderate.recommendation: Sample tip: Track which symptoms improved vs which remain for 1–2 weeks. Note timing relative to doses and any lifestyle factors. Bring this record to your clinician or pharmacist to discuss whether adjustment, waiting, or follow-up is appropriate.

Low.title: Low perceived effectiveness
Low.recommendation: Sample tip: Escalate to a clinician or pharmacist rather than stopping or increasing the dose yourself. List when the medicine was started, adherence, and other medicines/supplements. This prediction is a triage signal only, not a diagnosis.

0.label: Joint pain / hot flashes & patch-related effects
0.suggestion: Sample tip: Log joint pain, hot flashes, and whether you use a patch or hormone-related therapy. Note timing and severity. Discuss persistent or worsening symptoms with a clinician — do not adjust patch/dose on your own.

1.label: Skin / acne / facial dryness
1.suggestion: Sample tip: Photograph skin changes, list topicals/creams used, and avoid stacking new actives without advice. Seek urgent care for spreading rash, blistering, or facial/lip swelling.

2.label: Mild / generic side-effect language
2.suggestion: Sample tip: Even mild or vague effects are worth logging (date, severity 1–10, duration). Share the log at your next appointment so gradual changes are not missed.

3.label: Weight change & insomnia
3.suggestion: Sample tip: Track weight weekly and sleep quality (time to fall asleep, night waking). Discuss diet, timing of doses, and sleep hygiene with a pharmacist/clinician before stopping medicine.

4.label: Medication dosing / tiredness language
4.suggestion: Sample tip: Note when doses are taken and when tiredness appears. Ask a pharmacist whether timing with food or schedule changes are appropriate — do not change the prescribed dose yourself.

5.label: Pain, mood & sensory effects
5.suggestion: Sample tip: Record pain location/severity and any mood changes. Sudden severe pain, self-harm thoughts, or rapid mood shifts need prompt clinical advice.

6.label: Dry mouth, sexual & energy effects
6.suggestion: Sample tip: Dry mouth, libido/sexual changes, and low energy are common discussable side effects. Track them privately and raise them with a clinician; do not stop medicine abruptly without guidance.
